ourGain.point: Same-design carbon vs aluminum: B&H lists the Peak Design Travel Tripod at 2.81 lb in carbon and 3.44 lb in aluminum, a 0.63 lb (about 18%) saving on an otherwise identical tripod; DCW puts the general saving at around 25%.

Column-down height for every pick: Gitzo 55.3 in, Neewer 52 in, Peak Design 51.25 in, Heipi about 50 in, Leo 2.0 kit 44 in; the SIRUI 5C maker publishes none. That is the height you get without the stability loss of the column.

The weakest rating sets the real limit: the Neewer LT32 legs are rated 22 lb but its head 10 lb, the SIRUI 5C 8.8 lb, and Gitzo recommends its Traveler for 135mm lenses (200mm max). Chooser by heaviest lens: short zoom = SIRUI/Neewer; 70-200 = Peak Design/Heipi; DSLR + 70-200 or heavier = Gitzo or Leo 2.0.

Wind and wobble on a light carbon travel tripod: keep the column down, extend thickest sections first, hang the bag from the hook, spread legs wider; owners of the SIRUI 5C and Gitzo report wobble at full extension.
